title: Tommie Harris: OU's 2003 Lombardi Award Winner
question: Which Oklahoma defensive tackle won the Lombardi Award in 2003?
answer: Tommie Harris won the 2003 Lombardi Award as the nation's top lineman, becoming the third Sooner to win it. The Killeen, Texas, junior had been the runner-up in 2002 and returned to claim the honor.
summary: Tommie Harris won the 2003 Lombardi Award, the third Sooner to do so, after finishing runner-up in 2002. See his 2003 stats and how his NFL career unfolded.
body: Some players chase awards. Tommie Harris made a promise to win one. After finishing as the runner-up for the Lombardi Award in 2002, the Oklahoma defensive tackle came back as a junior in 2003 and claimed it, joining Lee Roy Selmon and Tony Casillas as the only Sooners to win the honor for the nation's best lineman or linebacker.

Harris, from Killeen, Texas, was the 12th Oklahoma player ever named a Lombardi finalist. He anchored a 2003 defense that sat near the top of nearly every national statistical category. His line that season included 37 tackles, 10 for loss, five sacks and a fumble recovery, impressive numbers for an interior lineman who drew constant double teams.

OU defensive line coach Jackie Shipp compared watching Harris to the days of Joe Washington, when everyone in the stadium waited to see what the star would do next. That 2003 defense was stacked: Harris was also a finalist for the Bednarik Award, which went to his teammate Teddy Lehman.

Harris played for Bob Stoops from 2001 to 2003, was named Big 12 Defensive Freshman of the Year in 2001 and earned first-team All-Big 12 honors. He also won the Bill Willis Trophy in 2003 and was a consensus All-American in 2002 and a unanimous one in 2003.

He skipped his senior year, and the Chicago Bears made him the 14th overall pick in the 2004 NFL Draft. Harris earned three Pro Bowl selections in Chicago. He later wrote a book, Endure, published in 2021.
